2609.09475.title: Distributed Physical Layer Authentication and Collaborative RSMA in Non-Terrestrial Networks via Graph Reinforcement Learning
2609.09475.paper_summary: Existing physical-layer authentication (PLA) schemes for non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) often rely on single-anchor verification, lack joint authentication-transmission design, and ignore tag privacy leakage under eavesdropping. In this paper, we consider passive, location-aware, static eavesdroppers without access to legitimate channel state information (CSI). Under this threat model, we propose secure adaptive federated authentication for multi-zone NTN systems (SAFA-MZ) that maximizes secrecy spectral efficiency (SSE) while ensuring authentication reliability, power limits, and coverage constraints. The main idea is to embed group-level authentication tags into a collaborative multi-layer rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) transmission structure. Private and common signals are jointly beamformed, artificial noise (AN) is used to reduce information leakage, and group differential privacy (GDP) protects tag information against inference attacks. In addition, users are grouped by semantic priority to allocate SSE based on information importance. We formulate a joint SSE maximization problem under authentication reliability and probabilistic secrecy constraints, optimizing high-altitude platform station (HAPS) placement, user association, and RSMA power allocation. The resulting problem is solved using a repair-based cross-entropy method (RCEM) and a graph-aware advantage actor-critic algorithm (GA2C). RCEM scales quadratically with the number of users, while GA2C scales linearly and achieves scalable, low-latency inference. Simulation results under both colluding and non-colluding eavesdroppers show that the proposed method improves average SSE by up to 135% over single-connect transmission and 21% over the scheme without AN. These results confirm SAFA-MZ offers a scalable and secure solution for dynamic NTN environments.
2609.09475.paper_summary_zh: 現有的非地面網絡 (NTN) 的物理層身份驗證 (PLA) 計劃通常依賴於單一錨點驗證，缺乏聯合身份驗證-傳輸設計，並忽視在竊聽下標籤隱私洩漏。在本文中，我們考慮被動的、位置感知的靜態竊聽者，且無法訪問合法的通道狀態信息 (CSI)。在這一威脅模型下，我們提出了一種針對多區域 NTN 系統的安全自適應聯邦身份驗證 (SAFA-MZ)，旨在最大化保密光譜效率 (SSE)，同時確保身份驗證的可靠性、功率限制和覆蓋約束。其主要思想是將群組級身份驗證標籤嵌入到協作的多層速率分割多重接入 (RSMA) 傳輸結構中。私有信號和公共信號共同進行波束形成，人工噪聲 (AN) 用於減少信息洩漏，群組差分隱私 (GDP) 保護標籤信息免受推斷攻擊。此外，根據信息的重要性，使用者按語義優先級分組，以分配 SSE。我們在身份驗證可靠性和概率保密約束下，制定了一個聯合 SSE 最大化問題，優化高空平台站 (HAPS) 的位置、用戶關聯和 RSMA 功率分配。所得到的問題使用基於修復的交叉熵方法 (RCEM) 和圖形感知優勢演員-評論者算法 (GA2C) 進行求解。RCEM 隨著用戶數量的增加而呈二次增長，而 GA2C 則呈線性增長，並實現可擴展的低延遲推斷。在共謀和非共謀竊聽者下的模擬結果顯示，所提出的方法在單連接傳輸上平均提高了 SSE 高達 135%，並在無 AN 的方案上提高了 21%。這些結果證實 SAFA-MZ 為動態 NTN 環境提供了一種可擴展且安全的解決方案。
